1	"""In-process build provenance records for registered resources.
2	
3	Each resource keeps at most one provenance record describing a single
4	build: the builder, a build number, a source summary digest and a list of
5	materials. Digests are normalized to lowercase and materials keep their
6	submission order. Nothing here is persisted: stopping or restarting the
7	service clears every record, no signatures are verified, and promotion
8	rules are unaffected.
9	"""
10	
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	import re
14	from dataclasses import dataclass
15	
16	#: A digest is exactly 64 hexadecimal characters; mixed case is accepted
17	#: but the digest is always stored and rendered in lowercase.
18	_DIGEST_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{64}")
19	
20	#: Text fields are non-empty and bounded by 256 Unicode code points.
21	MAX_TEXT_LENGTH = 256
22	
23	#: Fields accepted by the registration request; anything else is rejected.
24	_ALLOWED_FIELDS = frozenset(
25	    {"builder", "build_number", "source_digest", "materials"}
26	)
27	_REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("builder", "build_number", "source_digest", "materials")
28	_MATERIAL_FIELDS = frozenset({"name", "digest"})
29	
30	
31	class ProvenanceValidationError(ValueError):
32	    """A provenance payload failed field-level validation."""
33	
34	    def __init__(self, message: str) -> None:
35	        super().__init__(message)
36	        self.message = message
37	
38	
39	class ProvenanceError(ValueError):
40	    """A provenance operation could not proceed.
41	
42	    ``code`` is the stable, client-facing error code.
43	    """
44	
45	    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str) -> None:
46	        super().__init__(message)
47	        self.code = code
48	        self.message = message
49	
50	
51	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
52	class Material:
53	    """A single build material identified by name and digest."""
54	
55	    name: str
56	    digest: str
57	
58	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
59	        return {"name": self.name, "digest": self.digest}
60	
61	
62	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
63	class ProvenanceRecord:
64	    """The single build provenance record stored for a resource."""
65	
66	    builder: str
67	    build_number: str
68	    source_digest: str
69	    materials: tuple[Material, ...]
70	
71	    def to_dict(self, resource_id: str) -> dict[str, object]:
72	        return {
73	            "id": resource_id,
74	            "builder": self.builder,
75	            "build_number": self.build_number,
76	            "source_digest": self.source_digest,
77	            "materials": [material.to_dict() for material in self.materials],
78	        }
79	
80	
81	def _required_text(value: object, label: str) -> str:
82	    """Validate a required non-empty string of at most 256 code points."""
83	
84	    if not isinstance(value, str):
85	        raise ProvenanceValidationError(f"{label} must be a string.")
86	    if not value:
87	        raise ProvenanceValidationError(f"{label} must not be empty.")
88	    if len(value) > MAX_TEXT_LENGTH:
89	        raise ProvenanceValidationError(
90	            f"{label} must not exceed {MAX_TEXT_LENGTH} Unicode code points."
91	        )
92	    return value
93	
94	
95	def _require_digest(value: object, label: str) -> str:
96	    if not isinstance(value, str) or _DIGEST_PATTERN.fullmatch(value) is None:
97	        raise ProvenanceValidationError(
98	            f"{label} must be a 64-character hexadecimal string."
99	        )
100	    return value.lower()
101	
102	
103	def build_provenance_fields(
104	    payload: object,
105	) -> tuple[str, str, str, tuple[Material, ...]]:
106	    """Validate a decoded provenance payload and return normalized values.
107	
108	    Returns ``(builder, build_number, source_digest, materials)``. The
109	    source and material digests are normalized to lowercase and materials
110	    are returned in their submitted order (an empty material list is
111	    allowed). Repeated materials (same name and normalized digest) are a
112	    validation error.
113	    """
114	
115	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
116	        raise ProvenanceValidationError("Request body must be a JSON object.")
117	
118	    unknown_fields = set(payload) - _ALLOWED_FIELDS
119	    if unknown_fields:
120	        raise ProvenanceValidationError(
121	            f"Unknown field: {sorted(unknown_fields)[0]!r}."
122	        )
123	
124	    for field in _REQUIRED_FIELDS:
125	        if field not in payload:
126	            raise ProvenanceValidationError(
127	                f"Missing required field: {field!r}."
128	            )
129	
130	    builder = _required_text(payload["builder"], "Field 'builder'")
131	    build_number = _required_text(
132	        payload["build_number"], "Field 'build_number'"
133	    )
134	    source_digest = _require_digest(
135	        payload["source_digest"], "Field 'source_digest'"
136	    )
137	
138	    raw_materials = payload["materials"]
139	    if not isinstance(raw_materials, list):
140	        raise ProvenanceValidationError("Field 'materials' must be an array.")
141	
142	    materials: list[Material] = []
143	    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
144	    for position, raw_material in enumerate(raw_materials):
145	        if not isinstance(raw_material, dict):
146	            raise ProvenanceValidationError(
147	                f"Material at index {position} must be a JSON object."
148	            )
149	        material_unknown = set(raw_material) - _MATERIAL_FIELDS
150	        if material_unknown:
151	            raise ProvenanceValidationError(
152	                f"Unknown field: {sorted(material_unknown)[0]!r}."
153	            )
154	        for field in ("name", "digest"):
155	            if field not in raw_material:
156	                raise ProvenanceValidationError(
157	                    f"Material at index {position} is missing required "
158	                    f"field: {field!r}."
159	                )
160	        name = _required_text(
161	            raw_material["name"], "Material field 'name'"
162	        )
163	        digest = _require_digest(
164	            raw_material["digest"], "Material field 'digest'"
165	        )
166	        key = (name, digest)
167	        if key in seen:
168	            raise ProvenanceValidationError(
169	                "A material with the same name and digest is listed more "
170	                "than once."
171	            )
172	        seen.add(key)
173	        materials.append(Material(name=name, digest=digest))
174	
175	    return builder, build_number, source_digest, tuple(materials)
176	
177	
178	class ProvenanceStore:
179	    """Process-local storage of at most one provenance record per resource."""
180	
181	    def __init__(self) -> None:
182	        self._records: dict[str, ProvenanceRecord] = {}
183	
184	    def reset(self) -> None:
185	        self._records = {}
186	
187	    def remove_resource(self, resource_id: str) -> None:
188	        """Remove any provenance record for a resource.
189	
190	        An unknown id is a no-op.
191	        """
192	
193	        self._records.pop(resource_id, None)
194	
195	    def add(
196	        self, resource_id: str, payload: object
197	    ) -> tuple[ProvenanceRecord, bool]:
198	        """Validate and record the provenance for ``resource_id``.
199	
200	        Returns ``(record, created)`` where ``created`` is ``True`` for a
201	        first registration (HTTP 201) and ``False`` for an idempotent repeat
202	        of the exact same normalized content (HTTP 200).
203	
204	        Raises :class:`ProvenanceValidationError` for an invalid payload or
205	        :class:`ProvenanceError` with code ``provenance_conflict`` when a
206	        different record is already stored; the stored record is never
207	        overwritten.
208	        """
209	
210	        builder, build_number, source_digest, materials = (
211	            build_provenance_fields(payload)
212	        )
213	        record = ProvenanceRecord(
214	            builder=builder,
215	            build_number=build_number,
216	            source_digest=source_digest,
217	            materials=materials,
218	        )
219	
220	        existing = self._records.get(resource_id)
221	        if existing is not None:
222	            if existing == record:
223	                return existing, False
224	            raise ProvenanceError(
225	                "provenance_conflict",
226	                "A different provenance record is already registered for "
227	                "this resource.",
228	            )
229	
230	        self._records[resource_id] = record
231	        return record, True
232	
233	    def get(self, resource_id: str) -> ProvenanceRecord | None:
234	        return self._records.get(resource_id)

3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import re
6	import uuid
7	from dataclasses import dataclass
8	
9	#: The four resource categories exposed by the service.
10	CATEGORIES: tuple[str, ...] = ("code", "model", "dataset", "artifact")
11	_CATEGORY_VALUES = frozenset(CATEGORIES)
12	
13	_DIGEST_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{64}")
14	_ALLOWED_FIELDS = frozenset({"name", "category", "digest", "source"})
15	_REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("name", "category", "digest")
16	
17	
18	class ResourceValidationError(ValueError):
19	    """A registration payload failed field-level validation."""
20	
21	    def __init__(self, message: str) -> None:
22	        super().__init__(message)
23	        self.message = message
24	
25	
26	class DependencyError(ValueError):
27	    """A dependency relation could not be established.
28	
29	    ``code`` is the stable, client-facing error code.
30	    """
31	
32	    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str) -> None:
33	        super().__init__(message)
34	        self.code = code
35	        self.message = message

38	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
39	class Resource:
40	    """A single registered resource record."""
41	
42	    id: str
43	    name: str
44	    category: str
45	    digest: str
46	    source: str | None
47	
48	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
49	        return {
50	            "id": self.id,
51	            "name": self.name,
52	            "category": self.category,
53	            "digest": self.digest,
54	            "source": self.source,
55	        }
56	
57	
58	def _require_non_empty_string(value: object, label: str) -> str:
59	    if not isinstance(value, str):
60	        raise ResourceValidationError(f"{label} must be a string.")
61	    if not value.strip():
62	        raise ResourceValidationError(f"{label} must not be empty.")
63	    return value
64	
65	
66	def build_resource_fields(
67	    payload: object,
68	) -> tuple[str, str, str, str | None]:
69	    """Validate a decoded JSON payload and return normalized field values."""
70	
71	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
72	        raise ResourceValidationError("Request body must be a JSON object.")
73	
74	    unknown_fields = set(payload) - _ALLOWED_FIELDS
75	    if unknown_fields:
76	        raise ResourceValidationError(
77	            f"Unknown field: {sorted(unknown_fields)[0]!r}."
78	        )
79	
80	    for field in _REQUIRED_FIELDS:
81	        if field not in payload:
82	            raise ResourceValidationError(
83	                f"Missing required field: {field!r}."
84	            )
85	
86	    name = _require_non_empty_string(payload["name"], "Name")
87	
88	    category_raw = payload["category"]
89	    if not isinstance(category_raw, str):
90	        raise ResourceValidationError("Category must be a string.")
91	    category = category_raw.lower()
92	    if category not in _CATEGORY_VALUES:
93	        allowed = ", ".join(CATEGORIES)
94	        raise ResourceValidationError(
95	            f"Category must be one of: {allowed} (case-insensitive)."
96	        )
97	
98	    digest_raw = payload["digest"]
99	    if not isinstance(digest_raw, str) or _DIGEST_PATTERN.fullmatch(
100	        digest_raw
101	    ) is None:
102	        raise ResourceValidationError(
103	            "Digest must be a 64-character hexadecimal string."
104	        )
105	    # Hexadecimal digests are case-insensitive; store them canonically.
106	    digest = digest_raw.lower()
107	
108	    source: str | None = None
109	    if "source" in payload:
110	        source = _require_non_empty_string(payload["source"], "Source")
111	
112	    return name, category, digest, source

115	class ResourceStore:
116	    """Process-local, insertion-ordered resource storage."""
117	
118	    def __init__(self) -> None:
119	        self._resources: list[Resource] = []
120	        self._by_id: dict[str, Resource] = {}
121	        self._key_to_id: dict[tuple[str, str, str], str] = {}
122	        # resource id -> ids it directly depends on, and the reverse view.
123	        self._dependencies: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
124	        self._dependents: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
125	
126	    def reset(self) -> None:
127	        self._resources.clear()
128	        self._resources = []
129	        self._by_id = {}
130	        self._key_to_id = {}
131	        self._dependencies = {}
132	        self._dependents = {}
133	
134	    def list_all(self) -> list[Resource]:
135	        return list(self._resources)
136	
137	    def query(
138	        self,
139	        *,
140	        category: str | None = None,
141	        name: str | None = None,
142	        digest: str | None = None,
143	    ) -> list[Resource]:
144	        """Return matching resources in creation order.
145	
146	        ``category`` is compared case-insensitively, ``name`` is an exact
147	        string match and ``digest`` is compared against the stored lowercase
148	        form. Multiple conditions are AND-ed together.
149	        """
150	
151	        if category is None and name is None and digest is None:
152	            return list(self._resources)
153	
154	        matches: list[Resource] = []
155	        for resource in self._resources:
156	            if category is not None and resource.category != category.lower():
157	                continue
158	            if name is not None and resource.name != name:
159	                continue
160	            if digest is not None and resource.digest != digest:
161	                continue
162	            matches.append(resource)
163	        return matches
164	
165	    def get(self, resource_id: str) -> Resource | None:
166	        return self._by_id.get(resource_id)
167	
168	    def add(
169	        self, payload: object
170	    ) -> tuple[Resource | None, Resource | None]:
171	        """Validate and store a resource.
172	
173	        Returns ``(created, None)`` on success or ``(None, existing)`` when

175	        """

177	        name, category, digest, source = build_resource_fields(payload)
178	        key = (category, name, digest)
179	        existing_id = self._key_to_id.get(key)
180	        if existing_id is not None:

183	        resource = Resource(
184	            id=uuid.uuid4().hex,
185	            name=name,
186	            category=category,
187	            digest=digest,
188	            source=source,
189	        )
190	        self._resources.append(resource)
191	        self._by_id[resource.id] = resource
192	        self._key_to_id[key] = resource.id
193	        self._dependencies[resource.id] = set()
194	        self._dependents[resource.id] = set()
195	        return resource, None
196	
197	    def add_remote(
198	        self,
199	        *,
200	        name: str,
201	        category: str,
202	        digest: str,
203	        source: str | None,
204	        resource_id: str | None = None,
205	    ) -> Resource:
206	        """Store a resource resolved from a remote repository.
207	
208	        The caller has already validated the fields and matched the digest
209	        against the registry, so the record is constructed directly; the
210	        same uniqueness key is enforced defensively. When ``resource_id``
211	        is given it is reused (the caller already minted it during
212	        planning); otherwise a fresh id is generated.
213	        """
214	
215	        key = (category, name, digest)
216	        existing_id = self._key_to_id.get(key)
217	        if existing_id is not None:
218	            return self._by_id[existing_id]

220	        resource = Resource(
221	            id=resource_id if resource_id is not None else uuid.uuid4().hex,
222	            name=name,
223	            category=category,
224	            digest=digest,
225	            source=source,
226	        )
227	        self._resources.append(resource)
228	        self._by_id[resource.id] = resource
229	        self._key_to_id[key] = resource.id
230	        self._dependencies[resource.id] = set()
231	        self._dependents[resource.id] = set()
232	        return resource
233	
234	    def discard(self, resource_id: str) -> None:
235	        """Remove a resource that has no edges yet.
236	
237	        Used to roll back a resource created during an aborted operation.
238	        Only safe for resources with no dependencies or dependents.
239	        """
240	
241	        resource = self._by_id.pop(resource_id, None)
242	        if resource is None:
243	            return
244	        self._resources = [r for r in self._resources if r.id != resource_id]
245	        self._key_to_id.pop(
246	            (resource.category, resource.name, resource.digest), None
247	        )
248	        self._dependencies.pop(resource_id, None)
249	        self._dependents.pop(resource_id, None)
250	
251	    def remove(self, resource_id: str) -> Resource | None:
252	        """Remove a resource and every dependency edge touching it.
253	
254	        Returns the removed record, or ``None`` when the id is unknown.
255	        Edges the resource started and edges pointing at it disappear
256	        from both graph views; every other resource and edge is left
257	        untouched. The id is never reused by later registrations.
258	        """
259	
260	        resource = self._by_id.pop(resource_id, None)
261	        if resource is None:
262	            return None
263	        self._resources = [r for r in self._resources if r.id != resource_id]
264	        self._key_to_id.pop(
265	            (resource.category, resource.name, resource.digest), None
266	        )
267	        for dependency_id in self._dependencies.pop(resource_id, ()):
268	            dependents = self._dependents.get(dependency_id)
269	            if dependents is not None:
270	                dependents.discard(resource_id)
271	        for dependent_id in self._dependents.pop(resource_id, ()):
272	            dependencies = self._dependencies.get(dependent_id)
273	            if dependencies is not None:
274	                dependencies.discard(resource_id)

277	    # --- Dependencies ------------------------------------------------------
278	
279	    def _reachable(self, start: str, graph: dict[str, set[str]]) -> set[str]:
280	        """Transitive closure of ``start`` through ``graph`` (start excluded)."""
281	
282	        seen: set[str] = set()
283	        stack = list(graph.get(start, ()))
284	        while stack:
285	            node = stack.pop()
286	            if node in seen:
287	                continue
288	            seen.add(node)
289	            stack.extend(graph.get(node, ()))
290	        return seen
291	
292	    def _registration_order(self, ids: set[str]) -> list[str]:
293	        return [r.id for r in self._resources if r.id in ids]
294	
295	    def check_dependency(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> None:
296	        """Validate an edge without mutating the graph.
297	
298	        Raises :class:`DependencyError` with code ``duplicate_dependency``
299	        when the same-direction relation already exists, or
300	        ``dependency_cycle`` for a self loop or a relation that would
301	        introduce a cycle.
302	        """
303	
304	        if resource_id == dependency_id:
305	            raise DependencyError(
306	                "dependency_cycle", "A resource must not depend on itself."
307	            )
308	
309	        existing = self._dependencies.get(resource_id, ())
310	        if dependency_id in existing:
311	            raise DependencyError(
312	                "duplicate_dependency",
313	                "This dependency relation already exists.",
314	            )
315	
316	        # Adding resource_id -> dependency_id creates a cycle whenever
317	        # dependency_id can already reach resource_id.
318	        if resource_id in self._reachable(dependency_id, self._dependencies):
319	            raise DependencyError(
320	                "dependency_cycle",
321	                "This dependency would introduce a cycle.",
322	            )
323	
324	    def add_dependency(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> None:
325	        """Record that ``resource_id`` depends on ``dependency_id``.
326	
327	        Both resources must already be registered. Raises
328	        :class:`DependencyError` with code ``duplicate_dependency`` when the
329	        same-direction relation already exists, or ``dependency_cycle`` for a
330	        self loop or a relation that would introduce a cycle; in either case
331	        the graph is left unchanged.
332	        """
333	
334	        self.check_dependency(resource_id, dependency_id)
335	        self._dependencies[resource_id].add(dependency_id)
336	        self._dependents[dependency_id].add(resource_id)
337	
338	    def list_dependencies(self, resource_id: str) -> list[str]:
339	        """Return every reachable dependency id in registration order."""
340	
341	        return self._registration_order(
342	            self._reachable(resource_id, self._dependencies)
343	        )
344	
345	    def list_impact(self, resource_id: str) -> list[str]:
346	        """Return ids that directly or transitively depend on ``resource_id``.
347	
348	        The start resource itself is excluded; results are in registration
349	        order.
350	        """
351	
352	        return self._registration_order(
353	            self._reachable(resource_id, self._dependents)
354	        )

547	def _remove_resource_cascade(resource_id: str) -> None:
548	    """Remove every record keyed by ``resource_id`` across all stores.
549	
550	    Alerts, exemptions, SBOM and license data, provenance, policies,
551	    signatures, notifications, lifecycle state, chunk sessions with their
552	    assembled bytes, cross-repository references and dependency edges all
553	    disappear with the resource; derived read-only views (advisory
554	    summaries, component views, admission previews, risk scores) are
555	    computed on the fly and therefore reflect the removal immediately.
556	    Mirror sources, cache entries and other resources are never touched.
557	    """
558	
559	    vulnerability_store.remove_resource(resource_id)
560	    vulnerability_exception_store.remove_resource(resource_id)
561	    sbom_store.remove_resource(resource_id)
562	    provenance_store.remove_resource(resource_id)
563	    policy_store.remove_resource(resource_id)
564	    signature_store.remove_resource(resource_id)
565	    notification_store.remove_resource(resource_id)
566	    lifecycle_store.remove(resource_id)
567	    content_store.remove(resource_id)
568	    cross_reference_store.remove_resource(resource_id)
569	    store.remove(resource_id)

899	def _read_declared_body(environ: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[bytes | None, str | None]:
900	    """Read exactly the declared request body for content verification.
901	
902	    Returns ``(body, None)`` on success or ``(None, message)`` when the
903	    ``Content-Length`` header is missing or malformed, the stream cannot be
904	    read, or fewer bytes than declared are available. An explicitly declared
905	    length of zero is a valid empty body, not a missing one.
906	    """
907	
908	    raw_length = environ.get("CONTENT_LENGTH")
909	    if not isinstance(raw_length, str):
910	        return None, "Content-Length header is required."
911	    if _NON_NEGATIVE_INT_PATTERN.fullmatch(raw_length) is None:
912	        return None, "Content-Length header must be a non-negative integer."
913	    length = int(raw_length)
914	
915	    try:
916	        body = environ["wsgi.input"].read(length)
917	    except Exception:
918	        return None, "Request body could not be read."
919	    if not isinstance(body, (bytes, bytearray)) or len(body) != length:
920	        return None, "Request body is incomplete."
921	    return bytes(body), None

#: Process-local storage; records are not persisted across restarts.
store = ResourceStore()

#: Process-local chunk sessions and finalized content; also never persisted.
content_store = ContentStore()

#: Process-local lifecycle states; cleared on restart like everything else.
lifecycle_store = LifecycleStore()

#: Process-local vulnerability alerts; cleared on restart like the rest.
vulnerability_store = VulnerabilityStore()

#: Process-local vulnerability alert exemptions; cleared on restart like
#: the rest, and never persisted.
vulnerability_exception_store = VulnerabilityExceptionStore()

#: Process-local SBOM documents and license declarations; never persisted.
sbom_store = SbomStore()

#: Process-local build provenance records; never persisted.
provenance_store = ProvenanceStore()

#: Process-local admission policies and their read-only decisions; never
#: persisted and never materialized as records.
policy_store = PolicyStore()

#: Process-local global default admission policy; a single record consulted
#: only for resources without their own policy, never persisted.
default_policy_store = DefaultPolicyStore()

#: Process-local notification records; cleared on restart like the rest.
notification_store = NotificationStore()

#: Process-local image layer cache; entries and counters never persisted.
cache_store = LayerCacheStore()

#: Process-local image mirror registry; cleared on restart like everything.
mirror_store = MirrorStore()

#: Process-local mirror signature policies; cleared on restart like the
#: rest, and never persisted.
mirror_policy_store = MirrorPolicyStore()

#: Process-local latest mirror probe results; only the most recent result
#: per mirror is kept, nothing is persisted and the cache is never touched.
mirror_probe_store = ProbeStore()

#: Process-local cross-repository references; cleared on restart like the
#: rest.
cross_reference_store = CrossReferenceStore()

#: Process-local content signatures; cleared on restart like everything
#: else; verification is always computed on the fly and never recorded.

def reset_state() -> None:
    """Clear every in-process store (test and tooling helper)."""

    store.reset()
    content_store.reset()
    lifecycle_store.reset()
    vulnerability_store.reset()

#: Listing defaults and bounds.
DEFAULT_LIMIT = 50
MAX_LIMIT = 100
_LIST_PARAMS = frozenset({"category", "name", "digest", "limit", "cursor"})
_CATEGORY_VALUES = frozenset(CATEGORIES)
_DIGEST_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{64}")
_POSITIVE_INT_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[1-9][0-9]*")
_NON_NEGATIVE_INT_PATTERN = re.compile(r"0|[1-9][0-9]*")
_OCTET_STREAM_CONTENT_TYPE = "application/octet-stream"
_TOTAL_CHUNKS_HEADER = "HTTP_X_TOTAL_CHUNKS"
_CONTENT_DIGEST_HEADER = "HTTP_X_CONTENT_DIGEST"
_TOTAL_CHUNKS_HEADER_NAME = "X-Total-Chunks"
_CONTENT_DIGEST_HEADER_NAME = "X-Content-Digest"
_KEY_ID_HEADER = "HTTP_X_KEY_ID"
_SIGNATURE_HEADER = "HTTP_X_SIGNATURE"
_SIGNED_DIGEST_HEADER = "HTTP_X_SIGNED_DIGEST"
_KEY_ID_HEADER_NAME = "X-Key-Id"
_SIGNATURE_HEADER_NAME = "X-Signature"
_SIGNED_DIGEST_HEADER_NAME = "X-Signed-Digest"

#: Random per-process key so cursors cannot be forged and never survive a
#: restart; nothing here is persisted to disk.
_cursor_key = os.urandom(32)


class ListQueryError(ValueError):
    """A list request contained invalid query parameters or cursor."""


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ListQuery:
    category: str | None
    name: str | None
    digest: str | None
    limit: int
    offset: int
    paged: bool


def _cursor_signature(
    category: str, name: str, digest: str, limit: int, offset: int
) -> bytes:
    mac = hmac.new(_cursor_key, b"list-cursor-v1", hashlib.sha256)
    for part in (category, name, digest, str(limit)):
        encoded = part.encode("utf-8")
        mac.update(len(encoded).to_bytes(4, "big"))
        mac.update(encoded)
    mac.update(offset.to_bytes(8, "big"))
    return mac.digest()


def _b64encode(raw: bytes) -> str:
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).rstrip(b"=").decode("ascii")


def _b64decode(token: str) -> bytes:
    return base64.urlsafe_b64decode(token + "=" * (-len(token) % 4))


def _encode_cursor(
    category: str, name: str, digest: str, limit: int, offset: int
) -> str:
    return _b64encode(str(offset).encode("ascii")) + "." + _b64encode(
        _cursor_signature(category, name, digest, limit, offset)
    )


def _decode_cursor(
    raw: str, category: str, name: str, digest: str, limit: int
) -> int:
    """Return the offset encoded by a cursor.

    Raises :class:`ListQueryError` when the cursor is forged, corrupted or
    was issued for different filter conditions or limit.
    """

    token_b64, dot, sig_b64 = raw.partition(".")
    if not dot or not token_b64 or not sig_b64:
        raise ListQueryError("Cursor is malformed.")
    try:
        token = _b64decode(token_b64)
        sig = _b64decode(sig_b64)
    except (binascii.Error, ValueError):
        raise ListQueryError("Cursor is malformed.") from None

    if not token.isdigit() or token.startswith(b"0") or int(token) <= 0:
        raise ListQueryError("Cursor is malformed.")
    offset = int(token)

    expected = _cursor_signature(category, name, digest, limit, offset)
    if not hmac.compare_digest(sig, expected):
        raise ListQueryError("Cursor is not valid for this request.")
    return offset


def parse_list_query(query_string: str) -> ListQuery:
    """Parse and validate the query string for ``GET /resources``."""

    pairs = parse_qsl(query_string, keep_blank_values=True, strict_parsing=False)
    seen: set[str] = set()
    raw_values: dict[str, str] = {}
    for key, value in pairs:
        if key not in _LIST_PARAMS:
            raise ListQueryError(f"Unknown query parameter: {key!r}.")
        if key in seen:
            raise ListQueryError(f"Query parameter {key!r} must not be repeated.")
        seen.add(key)
        raw_values[key] = value

    category: str | None = None
    if "category" in raw_values:
        value = raw_values["category"]
        if value == "":
            raise ListQueryError("Category must not be empty.")
        if value.lower() not in _CATEGORY_VALUES:
            allowed = ", ".join(CATEGORIES)
            raise ListQueryError(
                f"Category must be one of: {allowed} (case-insensitive)."
            )
        category = value.lower()

    name: str | None = None
    if "name" in raw_values:
        value = raw_values["name"]
        # Exact, case-sensitive comparison; no trimming or folding.
        if value == "":
            raise ListQueryError("Name must not be empty.")
        name = value

    digest: str | None = None
    if "digest" in raw_values:
        value = raw_values["digest"]
        if _DIGEST_PATTERN.fullmatch(value) is None:
            raise ListQueryError(
                "Digest must be a 64-character hexadecimal string."
            )
        digest = value.lower()

    limit = DEFAULT_LIMIT
    if "limit" in raw_values:
        value = raw_values["limit"]
        if _POSITIVE_INT_PATTERN.fullmatch(value) is None:
            raise ListQueryError(
                f"Limit must be a positive integer no greater than {MAX_LIMIT}."
            )
        limit = int(value)
        if limit > MAX_LIMIT:
            raise ListQueryError(
                f"Limit must be a positive integer no greater than {MAX_LIMIT}."
            )

    offset = 0
    if "cursor" in raw_values:
        value = raw_values["cursor"]
        if value == "":
            raise ListQueryError("Cursor is malformed.")
        offset = _decode_cursor(
            value, category or "", name or "", digest or "", limit
        )

    paged = bool(seen)
    return ListQuery(
        category=category,
        name=name,
        digest=digest,
        limit=limit,
        offset=offset,
        paged=paged,
    )


def _parse_severity_query(
    query_string: str,
) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    """Parse the optional, single ``severity`` query parameter.

    Shared by the three advisory views and the per-resource alert listing:
    only ``severity`` is accepted, it must appear at most once, and its
    value must be one of the four levels (matched case-insensitively and
    normalized to lowercase). Returns ``(severity, None)`` -- with
    ``None`` when the parameter is absent -- or ``(None, message)`` for an
    unknown parameter, a repeated ``severity``, an empty value or an
    illegal level. The error messages are the stable, byte-for-byte
    wording every caller already answered with.
    """

    pairs = parse_qsl(
        query_string, keep_blank_values=True, strict_parsing=False
    )
    severity: str | None = None
    for key, value in pairs:
        if key != "severity":
            return None, f"Unknown query parameter: {key!r}."
        if severity is not None:
            return None, "Query parameter 'severity' must not be repeated."
        if value == "" or value.lower() not in SEVERITY_VALUES:
            return None, (
                "Severity must be one of: critical, high, medium, low "
                "(case-insensitive)."
            )
        severity = value.lower()
    return severity, None


def _handle_resources_get(
    environ: dict[str, Any], start_response: StartResponse
) -> Iterable[bytes]:
    try:
        query = parse_list_query(str(environ.get("QUERY_STRING", "")))
    except ListQueryError as exc:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            str(exc),
        )

    if not query.paged:
        # No filtering or pagination parameters: preserve the original shape.
        return _json_response(
            start_response,
            "200 OK",
            {"resources": [r.to_dict() for r in store.list_all()]},
            trailing_newline=True,
        )

    matched = store.query(
        category=query.category, name=query.name, digest=query.digest
    )
    page = matched[query.offset : query.offset + query.limit]
    next_offset = query.offset + len(page)
    next_cursor: str | None = None
    if next_offset < len(matched):
        next_cursor = _encode_cursor(
            query.category or "",
            query.name or "",
            query.digest or "",
            query.limit,
            next_offset,
        )

    return _json_response(
        start_response,
        "200 OK",
        {"resources": [r.to_dict() for r in page], "next_cursor": next_cursor},
        trailing_newline=True,
    )


def _json_response(
    start_response: StartResponse,
    status: str,
    payload: object,
    *,
    extra_headers: list[tuple[str, str]] | None = None,
    trailing_newline: bool = False,
) -> Iterable[bytes]:
    body = json.dumps(
        payload,
        ensure_ascii=False,
        separators=(",", ":"),
        allow_nan=False,
    ).encode("utf-8")
    if trailing_newline:
        body += b"\n"
    headers = [
        ("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8"),
        ("Content-Length", str(len(body))),
    ]
    if extra_headers:
        headers.extend(extra_headers)
    start_response(status, headers)
    return [body]


def _error(
    start_response: StartResponse,
    status: str,
    code: str,
    message: str,
    *,
    allowed: str | None = None,
    trailing_newline: bool = True,
) -> Iterable[bytes]:
    headers = []
    if allowed is not None:
        headers.append(("Allow", allowed))
    return _json_response(
        start_response,
        status,
        {"error": code, "message": message},
        extra_headers=headers,
        trailing_newline=trailing_newline,
    )


def _resource_response(
    start_response: StartResponse, status: str, resource: Resource
) -> Iterable[bytes]:
    return _json_response(
        start_response,
        status,
        resource.to_dict(),
        trailing_newline=True,
    )


def _read_body(environ: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
    try:
        length = int(environ.get("CONTENT_LENGTH") or 0)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        length = 0
    if length <= 0:
        return b""
    return environ["wsgi.input"].read(length)


def _handle_resources_post(
    environ: dict[str, Any], start_response: StartResponse
) -> Iterable[bytes]:
    raw = _read_body(environ)
    if not raw:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Request body is empty.",
        )
    try:
        payload = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Request body must be valid UTF-8 JSON.",
        )

    try:
        created, existing = store.add(payload)
    except ResourceValidationError as exc:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            exc.message,
        )

    if existing is not None:
        # Never overwrite or merge with the original record.
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "409 Conflict",
            "duplicate_resource",
            "A resource with the same category, name and digest already exists.",
        )

    assert created is not None
    return _resource_response(start_response, "201 Created", created)


def _remove_resource_cascade(resource_id: str) -> None:
    """Remove every record keyed by ``resource_id`` across all stores.

    Alerts, exemptions, SBOM and license data, provenance, policies,
    signatures, notifications, lifecycle state, chunk sessions with their
    assembled bytes, cross-repository references and dependency edges all
    disappear with the resource; derived read-only views (advisory
    summaries, component views, admission previews, risk scores) are
    computed on the fly and therefore reflect the removal immediately.
    Mirror sources, cache entries and other resources are never touched.
    """

    vulnerability_store.remove_resource(resource_id)
    vulnerability_exception_store.remove_resource(resource_id)
    sbom_store.remove_resource(resource_id)
    provenance_store.remove_resource(resource_id)
    policy_store.remove_resource(resource_id)
    signature_store.remove_resource(resource_id)
    notification_store.remove_resource(resource_id)
    lifecycle_store.remove(resource_id)
    content_store.remove(resource_id)
    cross_reference_store.remove_resource(resource_id)
    store.remove(resource_id)


def _handle_resource_item(
    method: str,
    environ: dict[str, Any],
    raw_id: str,
    start_response: StartResponse,
) -> Iterable[bytes]:
    if method not in ("GET", "DELETE"):
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "405 Method Not Allowed",
            "method_not_allowed",
            f"Method {method} is not allowed for this path.",
            allowed="DELETE, GET",
        )

    id_error = _validate_path_id(raw_id)
    if id_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", id_error
        )

    if method == "GET":
        resource = store.get(raw_id)
        if resource is None:
            return _error(
                start_response,
                "404 Not Found",
                "resource_not_found",
                "No resource exists with the requested id.",
            )
        return _resource_response(start_response, "200 OK", resource)

    # DELETE: a bodyless, parameterless request that unregisters the
    # resource and cascades to every record stored under its id.
    query_error = _query_parameter_error(environ)
    if query_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", query_error
        )
    body_error = _bodyless_request_error(environ)
    if body_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", body_error
        )

    resource = store.get(raw_id)
    if resource is None:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "404 Not Found",
            "resource_not_found",
            "No resource exists with the requested id.",
        )

    _remove_resource_cascade(raw_id)
    return _resource_response(start_response, "200 OK", resource)


def _validate_path_id(raw_id: str) -> str | None:
    """Return a stable error message for an invalid path id, else ``None``."""

    if not raw_id:
        return "Resource id must not be empty."
    if "/" in raw_id or "\\" in raw_id:
        return "Resource id must not contain path separators."
    return None


def _query_parameter_error(environ: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
    """Reject any query parameter on endpoints that declare none."""

    query_string = str(environ.get("QUERY_STRING", ""))
    if parse_qsl(query_string, keep_blank_values=True):
        return "This endpoint does not accept query parameters."
    return None


def _handle_dependencies_post(
    environ: dict[str, Any], raw_id: str, start_response: StartResponse
) -> Iterable[bytes]:
    id_error = _validate_path_id(raw_id)
    if id_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", id_error
        )

    query_error = _query_parameter_error(environ)
    if query_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", query_error
        )

    raw = _read_body(environ)
    if not raw:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Request body is empty.",
        )
    try:
        payload = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Request body must be valid UTF-8 JSON.",
        )

    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Request body must be a JSON object.",
        )
    unknown_fields = set(payload) - {"dependency_id"}
    if unknown_fields:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            f"Unknown field: {sorted(unknown_fields)[0]!r}.",
        )
    if "dependency_id" not in payload:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Missing required field: 'dependency_id'.",
        )
    dependency_id = payload["dependency_id"]
    if not isinstance(dependency_id, str) or not dependency_id:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Field 'dependency_id' must be a non-empty string.",
        )
    if "/" in dependency_id or "\\" in dependency_id:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Field 'dependency_id' must not contain path separators.",
        )

    # Both endpoints must already be registered; never auto-create.
    if store.get(raw_id) is None:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "404 Not Found",
            "resource_not_found",
            "No resource exists with the requested id.",
        )
    if store.get(dependency_id) is None:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "404 Not Found",
            "resource_not_found",
            "No resource exists with dependency_id.",
        )

    try:
        store.add_dependency(raw_id, dependency_id)
    except DependencyError as exc:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "409 Conflict",
            exc.code,
            exc.message,
        )

    return _json_response(
        start_response,
        "201 Created",
        {"resource_id": raw_id, "dependency_id": dependency_id},
        trailing_newline=True,
    )

def _handle_dependency_vulnerability_impact(
    method: str,
    environ: dict[str, Any],
    raw_id: str,
    start_response: StartResponse,
) -> Iterable[bytes]:
    if method != "GET":
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "405 Method Not Allowed",
            "method_not_allowed",
            f"Method {method} is not allowed for this path.",
            allowed="GET",
        )

    id_error = _validate_path_id(raw_id)
    if id_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", id_error
        )
    query_error = _query_parameter_error(environ)
    if query_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", query_error
        )
    if store.get(raw_id) is None:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "404 Not Found",
            "resource_not_found",
            "No resource exists with the requested id.",
        )

    # Read-only, computed on the fly: the start resource comes first, then
    # every reachable dependency in the same registration order the
    # dependency query uses; each resource appears exactly once and nothing
    # is recorded.
    impacts: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for resource_id in [raw_id, *store.list_dependencies(raw_id)]:
        alerts = vulnerability_store.list_for(resource_id)
        impacts.append(
            {
                "resource_id": resource_id,
                "advisory_count": len(alerts),
                "max_severity": max_severity(
                    alert.severity for alert in alerts
                ),
            }
        )

    return _json_response(
        start_response,
        "200 OK",
        {"impacts": impacts},
        trailing_newline=True,
    )


def _read_declared_body(environ: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[bytes | None, str | None]:
    """Read exactly the declared request body for content verification.

    Returns ``(body, None)`` on success or ``(None, message)`` when the
    ``Content-Length`` header is missing or malformed, the stream cannot be
    read, or fewer bytes than declared are available. An explicitly declared
    length of zero is a valid empty body, not a missing one.
    """

    raw_length = environ.get("CONTENT_LENGTH")
    if not isinstance(raw_length, str):
        return None, "Content-Length header is required."
    if _NON_NEGATIVE_INT_PATTERN.fullmatch(raw_length) is None:
        return None, "Content-Length header must be a non-negative integer."
    length = int(raw_length)

    try:
        body = environ["wsgi.input"].read(length)
    except Exception:
        return None, "Request body could not be read."
    if not isinstance(body, (bytes, bytearray)) or len(body) != length:
        return None, "Request body is incomplete."
    return bytes(body), None


def _handle_verify(
    method: str,
    environ: dict[str, Any],
    raw_id: str,
    start_response: StartResponse,
) -> Iterable[bytes]:
    if method != "POST":
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "405 Method Not Allowed",
            "method_not_allowed",
            f"Method {method} is not allowed for this path.",
            allowed="POST",
        )

    id_error = _validate_path_id(raw_id)
    if id_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", id_error
        )
    query_error = _query_parameter_error(environ)
    if query_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", query_error
        )

    content_type = str(environ.get("CONTENT_TYPE", ""))
    if content_type.lower() != _OCTET_STREAM_CONTENT_TYPE:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Content-Type must be application/octet-stream.",
        )

    body, body_error = _read_declared_body(environ)
    if body_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", body_error
        )
    assert body is not None

    resource = store.get(raw_id)
    if resource is None:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "404 Not Found",
            "resource_not_found",
            "No resource exists with the requested id.",
        )

    digest = hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()
    return _json_response(
        start_response,
        "200 OK",
        {"id": resource.id, "digest": digest, "valid": digest == resource.digest},
        trailing_newline=True,
    )


def _chunk_status_response(
    start_response: StartResponse,
    status: str,
    resource_id: str,
    index: int,
    total: int,
    digest: str,
    received: int,
) -> Iterable[bytes]:
    return _json_response(
        start_response,
        status,
        {
            "id": resource_id,
            "index": index,
            "total_chunks": total,
            "received_chunks": received,
            "digest": digest,
        },
        trailing_newline=True,
    )


def _handle_chunk(
    method: str,
    environ: dict[str, Any],
    raw_id: str,
    raw_index: str,
    start_response: StartResponse,
) -> Iterable[bytes]:
    if method != "POST":
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "405 Method Not Allowed",
            "method_not_allowed",
            f"Method {method} is not allowed for this path.",
            allowed="POST",
        )

    id_error = _validate_path_id(raw_id)
    if id_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", id_error
        )
    query_error = _query_parameter_error(environ)
    if query_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", query_error
        )

    # The chunk index is part of the path and must be a non-negative decimal
    # integer; anything else (including separators) is a bad request.
    if _NON_NEGATIVE_INT_PATTERN.fullmatch(raw_index) is None:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Chunk index must be a non-negative decimal integer.",
        )
    index = int(raw_index)

    content_type = str(environ.get("CONTENT_TYPE", ""))
    if content_type.lower() != _OCTET_STREAM_CONTENT_TYPE:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Content-Type must be application/octet-stream.",
        )

    raw_total = environ.get(_TOTAL_CHUNKS_HEADER)
    if not isinstance(raw_total, str) or not raw_total:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            f"{_TOTAL_CHUNKS_HEADER_NAME} header is required.",
        )
    if _POSITIVE_INT_PATTERN.fullmatch(raw_total) is None:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            f"{_TOTAL_CHUNKS_HEADER_NAME} header must be a positive integer.",
        )
    total = int(raw_total)
    if index >= total:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Chunk index must be smaller than the total chunk count.",
        )

    raw_digest = environ.get(_CONTENT_DIGEST_HEADER)
    if not isinstance(raw_digest, str) or _DIGEST_PATTERN.fullmatch(
        raw_digest
    ) is None:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            f"{_CONTENT_DIGEST_HEADER_NAME} header must be a 64-character "
            "hexadecimal digest.",
        )
    digest = raw_digest.lower()

    body, body_error = _read_declared_body(environ)
    if body_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", body_error
        )
    assert body is not None

    resource = store.get(raw_id)
    if resource is None:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "404 Not Found",
            "resource_not_found",
            "No resource exists with the requested id.",
        )

    if content_store.is_complete(raw_id):
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "409 Conflict",
            "content_already_complete",
            "Content for this resource is already complete.",
        )

    try:
        created, received = content_store.add_chunk(
            raw_id, total, digest, resource.digest, index, body
        )
    except ContentError as exc:
        return _error(
            start_response, "409 Conflict", exc.code, exc.message
        )

    return _chunk_status_response(
        start_response,
        "201 Created" if created else "200 OK",
        raw_id,
        index,
        total,
        digest,
        received,
    )

        return _error(

    id_error = _validate_path_id(raw_id)
    if id_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", id_error
        )
    query_error = _query_parameter_error(environ)
    if query_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", query_error
        )

    if store.get(raw_id) is None:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "404 Not Found",
            "resource_not_found",
            "No resource exists with the requested id.",
        )

    try:
        body = content_store.get_content(raw_id)
    except ContentError as exc:
        return _error(
            start_response, "409 Conflict", exc.code, exc.message
        )

    # The finalized artifact is returned as raw bytes only: no JSON wrapper
    # and no trailing newline.
    start_response(
        "200 OK",
        [
            ("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream"),
            ("Content-Length", str(len(body))),
        ],
    )
    return [body]

def _handle_lifecycle_post(
    environ: dict[str, Any], raw_id: str, start_response: StartResponse
) -> Iterable[bytes]:
    id_error = _validate_path_id(raw_id)
    if id_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", id_error
        )
    query_error = _query_parameter_error(environ)
    if query_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", query_error
        )

    raw = _read_body(environ)
    if not raw:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Request body is empty.",
        )
    try:
        payload = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Request body must be valid UTF-8 JSON.",
        )

    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Request body must be a JSON object.",
        )
    unknown_fields = set(payload) - {"state", "reason"}
    if unknown_fields:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            f"Unknown field: {sorted(unknown_fields)[0]!r}.",
        )
    if "state" not in payload:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Missing required field: 'state'.",
        )
    target = payload["state"]
    if not isinstance(target, str) or target not in STATE_VALUES:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Field 'state' must be one of: staged, released, withdrawn, "
            "quarantined (case-sensitive).",
        )

    reason: str | None = None
    if "reason" in payload:
        value = payload["reason"]
        if not isinstance(value, str):
            return _error(
                start_response,
                "400 Bad Request",
                "invalid_request",
                "Field 'reason' must be a string.",
            )
        if value == "":
            return _error(
                start_response,
                "400 Bad Request",
                "invalid_request",
                "Field 'reason' must not be empty.",
            )
        if len(value) > MAX_REASON_LENGTH:
            return _error(
                start_response,
                "400 Bad Request",
                "invalid_request",
                f"Field 'reason' must not exceed {MAX_REASON_LENGTH} "
                "Unicode code points.",
            )
        reason = value
    if target in REASON_REQUIRED_STATES and reason is None:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            f"Field 'reason' is required when the target state is "
            f"{target!r}.",
        )

    if store.get(raw_id) is None:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "404 Not Found",
            "resource_not_found",
            "No resource exists with the requested id.",
        )

    current = lifecycle_store.get(raw_id)
    if (current.state, target) == ("staged", "released"):
        # Promotion requires assembled content and healthy dependencies.
        if not content_store.is_complete(raw_id):
            return _error(
                start_response,
                "409 Conflict",
                "content_not_complete",
                "Content for this resource is not complete.",
            )
        for dependency_id in store.list_dependencies(raw_id):
            if lifecycle_store.get(dependency_id).state in BLOCKING_STATES:
                return _error(
                    start_response,
                    "409 Conflict",
                    "dependency_blocked",
                    "A dependency of this resource is withdrawn or "
                    "quarantined.",
                )

    try:
        record = lifecycle_store.apply(current, target, reason)
    except LifecycleError as exc:
        return _error(
            start_response, "409 Conflict", exc.code, exc.message
        )

    # ``apply`` returns the very same record for an idempotent repeat; only a
    # real transition is stored, so a repeat never adds a record.
    if record is not current:
        lifecycle_store.set(raw_id, record)
    return _lifecycle_response(start_response, "200 OK", raw_id, record)


def _handle_lifecycle(
    method: str,

    if method == "GET":
        return _handle_lifecycle_get(environ, raw_id, start_response)
    if method == "POST":
        return _handle_lifecycle_post(environ, raw_id, start_response)
    return _error(
        start_response,
        "405 Method Not Allowed",
        "method_not_allowed",
        f"Method {method} is not allowed for this path.",
        allowed="GET, POST",
    )


def _handle_release_blockers(
    method: str,
    environ: dict[str, Any],
    raw_id: str,
    start_response: StartResponse,
) -> Iterable[bytes]:
    if method != "GET":
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "405 Method Not Allowed",
            "method_not_allowed",
            f"Method {method} is not allowed for this path.",
            allowed="GET",
        )

    id_error = _validate_path_id(raw_id)
    if id_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", id_error
        )
    query_error = _query_parameter_error(environ)
    if query_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", query_error
        )
    if store.get(raw_id) is None:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "404 Not Found",
            "resource_not_found",
            "No resource exists with the requested id.",
        )

    # Read-only, computed on the fly from the very same promotion checks as
    # the staged -> released transition, but never short-circuiting: both
    # reason codes and every blocked dependency are reported. Nothing is
    # recorded and no existing state is touched.
    content_complete = content_store.is_complete(raw_id)
    reasons: list[str] = []
    if not content_complete:
        reasons.append("content_not_complete")

    blockers: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for dependency_id in store.list_dependencies(raw_id):
        state = lifecycle_store.get(dependency_id).state
        if state in BLOCKING_STATES:
            blockers.append({"resource_id": dependency_id, "state": state})
    if blockers:
        reasons.append("dependency_blocked")

    return _json_response(
        start_response,
        "200 OK",
        {
            "id": raw_id,
            "blocked": bool(reasons),
            "reasons": reasons,
            "blockers": blockers,
            "content_complete": content_complete,
        },
        trailing_newline=True,
    )

    id_error = _validate_path_id(raw_id)
    if id_error is not None:
        return _error(
            start_response, "400 Bad Request", "invalid_request", id_error
        )
    query_error = _query_parameter_error(environ)

    raw = _read_body(environ)
    if not raw:
        return _error(
            start_response,

            "Request body is empty.",
        )
    try:
        payload = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            "Request body must be valid UTF-8 JSON.",
        )

    # Validate the whole body before touching any store, so a bad request
    # can never leave a partial exemption.
    try:
        build_exception_fields(payload)
    except VulnerabilityExceptionValidationError as exc:
        return _error(
            start_response,
            "400 Bad Request",
            "invalid_request",
            exc.message,
        )

    if store.get(raw_id) is None:
        return _error(
            start_response,

    try:

            start_response, http_status, exc.code, exc.message

1	"""Cross-repository references and remote resource resolution.
2	
3	A cross-reference hangs off a locally registered resource (the
4	*dependent*) and points at a resource living in another repository. A
5	record carries four client-supplied keys:
6	
7	- ``repository`` names the remote repository; the first time a repository
8	  name is seen it is bound to the ``upstream`` address;
9	- ``upstream`` is the absolute ``http``/``https`` base address of the
10	  remote repository;
11	- ``remote_id`` identifies the resource within that repository;
12	- ``digest`` is the 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest the caller
13	  expects the remote resource to have.
14	
15	On registration the remote repository is contacted at
16	``<upstream>/resources/<remote_id>`` and the returned metadata must carry
17	``name``, ``category``, ``digest`` and ``source``. The reported digest is
18	compared against the expected one. On success a local resource is
19	created (or an identical existing one reused) and a same-direction
20	dependency edge from the local resource to the resolved one is
21	established, so resolved edges participate in the existing dependency
22	topology and impact analysis.
23	
24	Registration is staged so every detectable failure happens before any
25	state changes:
26	
27	1. :meth:`CrossReferenceStore.check_prerequisites` rejects a repository
28	   bound to a different upstream and a repeated ``(repository,
29	   remote_id)`` pair;
30	2. the remote repository is contacted and its metadata validated;
31	3. :meth:`CrossReferenceStore.plan` resolves the local identity (reuse or
32	   create) and pre-validates the dependency edge (self loop, duplicate
33	   edge, cycle);
34	4. the caller writes the resolved metadata to the shared layer cache
35	   (which may still raise ``cache_conflict``);
36	5. :meth:`CrossReferenceStore.commit` creates the resource, adds the edge
37	   and stores the reference record atomically.
38	
39	Everything lives in the current process memory: records, bindings,
40	resources and edges are lost on restart and nothing is written to a
41	file. Batching and concurrency are intentionally out of scope.
42	"""
43	
44	from __future__ import annotations
45	
46	import json
47	import re
48	import urllib.error
49	import urllib.request
50	import uuid
51	from dataclasses import dataclass
52	from urllib.parse import quote, urlsplit
53	
54	from .resources import (
55	    CATEGORIES,
56	    DependencyError,
57	    Resource,
58	    ResourceStore,
59	)
60	
61	#: Fetch timeout in seconds for contacting an upstream repository.
62	DEFAULT_FETCH_TIMEOUT = 10.0
63	
64	_DIGEST_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{64}")
65	_ALLOWED_FIELDS = frozenset(
66	    {"repository", "upstream", "remote_id", "digest"}
67	)
68	_REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("repository", "upstream", "remote_id", "digest")
69	_CATEGORY_VALUES = frozenset(CATEGORIES)
70	#: Keys a remote ``/resources/<id>`` document must contain.
71	_REMOTE_FIELDS = ("name", "category", "digest", "source")
72	
73	
74	class CrossReferenceValidationError(ValueError):
75	    """A registration payload failed field-level validation."""
76	
77	    def __init__(self, message: str) -> None:
78	        super().__init__(message)
79	        self.message = message
80	
81	
82	class CrossReferenceError(Exception):
83	    """A cross-reference could not be established.
84	
85	    ``code`` is the stable, client-facing error code and ``http_status``
86	    the status line the HTTP layer should answer with.
87	    """
88	
89	    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str, *, http_status: int) -> None:
90	        super().__init__(message)
91	        self.code = code
92	        self.message = message
93	        self.http_status = http_status
94	
95	
96	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
97	class CrossReference:
98	    """A single registered cross-repository reference."""
99	
100	    resource_id: str
101	    repository: str
102	    upstream: str
103	    remote_id: str
104	    digest: str
105	
106	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
107	        # ``resource_id`` first, then the four registration keys in their
108	        # documented order.
109	        return {
110	            "resource_id": self.resource_id,
111	            "repository": self.repository,
112	            "upstream": self.upstream,
113	            "remote_id": self.remote_id,
114	            "digest": self.digest,
115	        }

118	def _require_non_empty_string(value: object, label: str) -> str:
119	    if not isinstance(value, str):
120	        raise CrossReferenceValidationError(f"{label} must be a string.")
121	    if not value.strip():
122	        raise CrossReferenceValidationError(f"{label} must not be empty.")
123	    return value

126	def _build_upstream(value: object) -> str:
127	    upstream = _require_non_empty_string(value, "Upstream")
128	    parts = urlsplit(upstream)
129	    # A network location is required so relative addresses or bare schemes
130	    # are rejected; only http and https are supported.
131	    if parts.scheme not in ("http", "https") or not parts.netloc:
132	        raise CrossReferenceValidationError(

134	        )

138	def build_cross_reference_fields(
139	    payload: object,
140	) -> tuple[str, str, str, str]:
141	    """Validate a decoded JSON payload and return normalized field values."""
142	
143	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
144	        raise CrossReferenceValidationError(
145	            "Request body must be a JSON object."
146	        )

148	    unknown_fields = set(payload) - _ALLOWED_FIELDS
149	    if unknown_fields:

151	            f"Unknown field: {sorted(unknown_fields)[0]!r}."
152	        )
153	
154	    for field in _REQUIRED_FIELDS:
155	        if field not in payload:
156	            raise CrossReferenceValidationError(
157	                f"Missing required field: {field!r}."
158	            )
159	
160	    repository = _require_non_empty_string(
161	        payload["repository"], "Repository"
162	    )
163	    upstream = _build_upstream(payload["upstream"])
164	    remote_id = _require_non_empty_string(payload["remote_id"], "Remote id")
165	    if "/" in remote_id or "\\" in remote_id:
166	        raise CrossReferenceValidationError(
167	            "Remote id must not contain path separators."
168	        )
169	
170	    digest_raw = payload["digest"]
171	    if not isinstance(digest_raw, str) or _DIGEST_PATTERN.fullmatch(
172	        digest_raw
173	    ) is None:
174	        raise CrossReferenceValidationError(
175	            "Digest must be a 64-character hexadecimal string."
176	        )
177	    # Hexadecimal digests are case-insensitive; compare canonically.
178	    digest = digest_raw.lower()
179	
180	    return repository, upstream, remote_id, digest
181	
182	
183	def _remote_resource_url(upstream: str, remote_id: str) -> str:
184	    # Mirror the mirror-source joining rule (trailing slash stripped) and
185	    # percent-encode the remote id segment.
186	    return (
187	        upstream.rstrip("/")
188	        + "/resources/"
189	        + quote(remote_id, safe="")
190	    )
191	
192	
193	def fetch_remote_resource(
194	    upstream: str,
195	    remote_id: str,
196	    *,
197	    timeout: float = DEFAULT_FETCH_TIMEOUT,
198	) -> bytes:
199	    """GET ``<upstream>/resources/<remote_id>`` and return the raw body.
200	
201	    Raises :class:`CrossReferenceError` with code ``remote_unreachable``
202	    when the upstream cannot be contacted, times out or answers a non-200
203	    status.
204	    """
205	
206	    url = _remote_resource_url(upstream, remote_id)
207	    request = urllib.request.Request(url, method="GET")
208	    try:
209	        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout) as response:
210	            if getattr(response, "status", response.getcode()) != 200:
211	                raise CrossReferenceError(

213	                    "Upstream repository did not return the resource.",
